newsitem.title: UK: British bookmakers cut odds against Conservative win.
newsitem.headline: British bookmakers cut odds against Conservative win.

text.p: British bookmakers William Hill said on Thursday they had cut their odds against the ruling Conservative party winning the May 1 election to 7-1 from 9-1 after punters started backing the beleaguered government.

The firm shortened the odds on a Conservative win to the shortest level since the election campaign began three weeks ago after opinion polls suggested the party was reducing the large gap with the main opposition Labour party.
"This is the first indication we may take some serious cash for the Conservatives," said a spokesman for Hill's, which adjusted the odds of a Labour win to 2-9 on from 1-5 on.

A MORI poll in Thursday's Times newspaper showed the Conservatives just 15 points adrift of Labour, compared with 27 points last week. The survey gave the ruling party 34 percent support against 49 percent for Labour.
The Conservatives were quoted at 7-2 to be the largest single party, in from 4-1. Hill's adjusted Labour's odds to 1-6 on from 1-7 on to be the single largest party.
The bookmaker maintained its offer of 4-1 odds on a hung parliament.
